body.x: GLEC Co., Ltd. (Co-CEOs Deokho Kevin Kang and Eun-woo Stella Kim) announced that it will participate in CES 2026, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), as part of the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion.

GLEC is a Korean company that has developed solutions to measure, verify, and reduce carbon emissions in compliance with international logistics standards. The company explained that it provides carbon management systems recognized for global quality and reliability, centered on carbon data standardization in accordance with ISO 14083 and the GLEC Framework.

At CES 2026, GLEC was selected as a CES Innovation Award winner in the Supply & Logistics category for its proprietary carbon management solution, gaining global recognition for the competitiveness of its technology and products. Building on this achievement, GLEC aims to lead the decarbonization of the logistics industry and to drive data-driven management grounded in technological innovation and international standards compliance.

At this year’s CES, GLEC will present the Innovation Award–winning digital tachograph ‘GLEC DTG Series 5’ as its flagship product. Using AIoT technology, the device integrates real-time risk analysis, driving behavior evaluation, and comprehensive vehicle condition monitoring.

The distinguishing feature of GLEC DTG Series 5 is its ability to predict not only carbon data but also accident and risky driving patterns, enabled by GLEC’s proprietary AI engine embedded directly in the hardware. As a result, the solution is expected to deliver tangible benefits, including improved driver safety, reduced accident-related costs, insurance linkage, and extended vehicle lifespan. Designed with a globally scalable standard architecture, it has also received high evaluations for versatility.

body.cap: GLEC Carbon DTG and GLEC LCS | Image provided by GLEC

body.x: In addition, GLEC will introduce ‘GLEC Carbon DTG,’ which precisely calculates vehicle-level carbon emissions by collecting and analyzing real-time data, including fuel consumption per vehicle, driving distance, empty mileage, and driver behavior, alongside conventional tachograph functions. The company will also present ‘GLEC LCS,’ an API-based global logistics carbon-emission calculation and verification solution, as another example of its technological capabilities.

A GLEC official said, “Our solutions form an innovative platform that supports everything from carbon emission measurement and reduction planning to safety management for logistics companies, based on quantitative data,” adding, “Our goal is to set a new standard for the global logistics industry by leveraging an integrated technology portfolio that combines hardware, APIs, and services.”

The official continued, “This CES will serve as an important opportunity to prove the innovativeness of GLEC’s technology and clearly communicate our commercialization models and customer value,” and added, “Through this, we plan to build networks with overseas logistics companies, transport operators, fleet managers, related solution developers, and investors, while laying the groundwork for global joint projects and data verification systems.”

Incheon Metropolitan City and the Incheon Free Economic Zone Authority announced that they will establish the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion in the LVCC North Hall at CES 2026, showcasing Incheon’s urban vision and innovative technologies as the city evolves from smart city development into the AI era. By linking various exhibition programs—including the 10 companies participating in the INCHEON-IFEZ Pavilion, Eureka Park, global pavilions, and the CES Innovation Award Showcase—the organizations will support the participation of 51 Incheon-based innovative companies at CES. Notably, 14 companies received CES Innovation Awards across 17 categories, marking a record-high achievement and demonstrating the technological competitiveness and global growth potential of Incheon’s innovation companies.
